title: Landings, Column Rows, Script Spacing, One Signal & Smooth Details
description: Snap events that announce the landed card, multicol rows, CJK auto-spacing, style-query state and an animatable details element.

drops.title: The Card That Knows It Landed
drops.description: A snap carousel that runs its entry animation from the scroller's own scrollsnapchange event.
drops.concept: Scroll containers now fire scrollsnapchanging when a new snap target is being selected and scrollsnapchange once the scroll settles on it. That removes the usual IntersectionObserver plus scroll-maths scaffolding behind carousels: the newly landed card simply gets a class the moment the platform decides it has landed. The drop shows a horizontal rail, a vertical list and a third scroller driving a remote strip, with a live event log and an observer fallback where the events are missing.
drops.source: MDN Web Docs — Element: scrollsnapchange event

interaction.mouse: Drag or wheel-scroll the rails; the landed card scales up and runs its own timeline
interaction.click: Switch scroll-snap-type between mandatory and proximity, and retime the transition
interaction.touch: Flick the rails; the same two events fire for touch scrolling

drops.title: Columns That Wrap Into Rows
drops.description: column-height caps a row of columns; column-wrap sends the overflow into a new row instead of off the side.
drops.concept: Before Multi-column Level 2, a height-constrained multicol container pushed its surplus columns sideways and quietly became a horizontal scroller. Declaring column-height fixes the height of one row of columns, and column-wrap: wrap starts the remainder as a fresh row in the block direction, separated by an ordinary row gap. The drop runs three flows — a long article, a dense caption grid and a block-direction carousel — and reports the live column count, row count and whether a sideways scroller still exists.
drops.source: CSS Multi-column Layout Module Level 2 editor's draft (shipped in Chrome 145)

interaction.mouse: Drag the column width, height and gap sliders and watch the rows reflow
interaction.click: Toggle between wrap and nowrap to compare the new behaviour with the legacy sideways overflow
interaction.touch: Sliders and toggles are touch-sized; panels stack on narrow screens

drops.title: The Space Between Scripts
drops.description: text-autospace adds the eighth of an em that belongs between CJK characters and Latin letters or digits.
drops.concept: East Asian typesetting has always put a sliver of air where ideographs meet Latin letters or numerals, and until recently the web could only fake it with inserted spans. text-autospace asks the shaper to do it, so the text stays one selectable run. Unicode's report defines the wide/narrow character classes the spacing is inserted between. The drop sets three mixed-script specimens with the property off, on and hand-simulated, probes which values the engine actually accepts, and measures the real width difference on an unwrapped line.
drops.source: Unicode UTR #59 — East Asian Spacing (the algorithm CSS text-autospace applies)

interaction.mouse: Drag type size and letter-spacing to see the spacing scale with the em
interaction.click: Pick the value applied to the second row; unsupported longhands say so and fall back to normal
interaction.touch: Specimens stack and stay legible at phone width

drops.title: One Property, Five Reactions
drops.description: Flip one custom property on a card and its dot, label, icon, bar and footnote all restyle themselves.
drops.concept: A container style query matches on a custom property of an ancestor, so a component can keep all of its state in one place and let descendants react. Here hover and press set --state on the card, and @container style(--state: warm | hot | done) restyles five children with no class toggling and no inline styles. Nested containers show the nearest ancestor winning, and the drop probes support by injecting a rule and reading back whether it matched.
drops.source: OpenReplay — Using CSS if() vs container style queries

interaction.mouse: Hover a card to warm it, press to drive it hot, click to lock it as settled
interaction.click: Pin every card to one state from the panel, or retime the transition
interaction.touch: Tapping a card locks its state; the toolbar row reacts as a whole

drops.title: Details That Open Smoothly
drops.description: ::details-content, allow-discrete and interpolate-size turn the native disclosure widget into an animated accordion.
drops.concept: The contents of a closed details element were never a box you could address, which is why every accordion on the web was rebuilt with a wrapper div and a measured pixel height. ::details-content exposes that box, transition-behavior: allow-discrete keeps content-visibility painted while the panel collapses, and interpolate-size lets the height animate to auto. The drop runs an exclusive FAQ accordion, a drawer that animates inline-size instead, and a nested disclosure tree.
drops.source: Chrome for Developers — More options for styling <details>

interaction.mouse: Click any summary; the panel animates to the height of its own content
interaction.click: Retime and re-ease the transition, or turn the exclusive accordion name off to open several at once
interaction.touch: Summaries are full-width tap targets; the sideways drawers work the same way
